did_you_know.text: Samson tore out the doors of the gate of Gaza, along with the two doorposts and the bar. He carried them on his shoulders and took them to the mountain facing Hebron.
The rulers of the Philistines offered Delilah a large sum of money if she would seduce Samson and discover the source of his great strength and how he could be captured.
On the third attempt, Samson told Delilah that he would become weak if she wove the seven locks of his hair into a web. But even then, he broke free when he woke up.
Samson revealed his secret to Delilah: no razor had ever touched his head because he had been a Nazirite dedicated to God from birth. He linked the shaving of his hair to the loss of his strength.
After his hair was shaved off, Samson did not know that the LORD had left him. He thought he would escape as he had before, but the Philistines seized him.
The Philistines gouged out Samson’s eyes, took him down to Gaza, bound him with bronze shackles, and forced him to grind grain in the prison.
Despite his captivity and humiliation, Samson’s hair began to grow back after it had been shaved off.
All the rulers of the Philistines were gathered in the temple of Dagon, and about three thousand men and women were sitting on the roof, watching Samson entertain them.
At his death, Samson brought down the temple on the rulers and all the people inside. The number he killed at his death was greater than the number he had killed during his lifetime.

His brothers and his father’s household carried Samson away and buried him between Zorah and Eshtaol, in the tomb of his father Manoah. The verse concludes by stating that Samson had judged Israel for twenty years.
